scope: Common StateClone ownership of a finite original native copy slot, including retained failed controls, cancellation, explicit wait/poll and retry.
defect: A failed/cancelled StateCell and retained Ticket/Draft kept route/copy ordinals after native cleanup and explicit cold rearm. Old wait could observe a newer copy; old cancellation/destruction could cancel or retire it. Typed take also freed an Unavailable copy while its public owner remained valid.
fix: Revoke existing StateCell route/copy ownership before original cancellation/fatal-error retirement; every ticket native entry validates its retained record's ownership before access/observer admission. Preserve pending publication semantics and first candidate failure; successful writer transfer clears both native indices. Unavailable preserves original live Submission and retry ownership. No public generation API or StateRecord layout change.

actual_tests.limits: Original real CPU F2 copy, sequential slot reuse and actual output-reader exclusion. Fatal/Unavailable diagnostics are test-only transparent observation boundaries after original CPU wait success; no GPU pending/error claim.

final_before: The same final four new tests against the retained old product/old header execute with3 failing cases and1 passing reader-exclusivity control. Old fatal-observation failure includes its original Bad expected access exception; the unexecuted remainder of that old case is not claimed as coverage.
final_after: 37 actual StateVersions/StateClone cases, zero failures/skips, including six old-control actions, fatal poll and wait, original extra-reader try_write Unavailable and one diagnostic Unavailable through poll/wait. Original observer-close and schema-extent neighbors remain included.

freeze.scope: Revoke the existing StateCell pending route/copy ownership before cancellation/fatal failure permits finite native slot reuse.
ownership_rules: pending denotes an unpublished schema member; route/copy jointly name only its currently accepted native copy.
cancel_copy executes under the existing StateStore monitor, exchanges route/copy to UINT32_MAX before calling original driver.cancel, preserves pending and the first candidate failure.
Every old Ticket native access proves its exact StateCell still owns its route/copy; failed/closed draft prechecks release any still-owned copy before returning original status.
Explicit wait validates ownership before observer pinning; original native wait remains outside the monitor and uses the existing per-slot wait lock.
Non-Unavailable native wait/take failures revoke and abandon their copy; Unavailable retains the same owner and original live Submission for retry, including the typed take wait-error branch.
Successful take clears both route/copy before transferring its existing draft reference and writer permission to StateWriter.
Store close/drain, actual native retirement, collect/rearm and observer exclusion remain in their original implementations.

reviewer_activity.method: Read actual frozen/current product source, full changed test bodies, no-index product diffs, test design and existing root expected-red result; verify exact SHA256 identities.

ownership_proof: StateRecord refs retain the exact old draft record while any Draft/Ticket/Writer exists. A failed/cancelled record cannot reopen, and each entry has at most one accepted pending clone. Clearing its route/copy therefore revokes that old control without a new public generation API.

cancel_copy runs only under the existing StateStore monitor, captures both original indices by exchange to UINT32_MAX before calling the original driver.cancel, and preserves pending. pending continues to mean an unpublished member, independently of whether a native copy remains controlled.

StateDraft::cancel revokes all still-owned copy cells. CloneTicket::request_cancel and its destructor forward only when the current cell still matches pending/route/copy. Repeated stale actions affect only their retained old record, never a reused native slot.

require_copy checks open_draft before any original ticket wait/take observation and cancels an entry still owned by a now-failed/closed candidate. No successful/native-ready result can reopen that failed record.

Explicit wait admits observer pin only after require_copy under the same store monitor. The original native wait remains outside the store lock and under its existing per-slot wait_lock. Cancellation during observation may revoke the cell, but observer count prevents native replacement until every observer leaves.

On fatal non-Unavailable native wait, observer removal, first-failure storage and owned-copy revocation occur under the store monitor. On fatal take, native cleanup and public owner revocation are within the same store critical section, leaving no reuse admission gap.

Unavailable preserves the same cell identity and accepted native Submission/live slot. The header now also avoids cleanup in its sub.wait Unavailable branch, so public retry ownership cannot outlive a freed native episode. Persistent original Unavailable is returned on each original wait; this code does not substitute success or publish output after an error.

Successful take clears both route/copy and transfers the existing draft reference with the original WriteLease. StateWriter publication/completion and its schema extent/identity checks remain unchanged.

StateStore::drain first closes admission and pins all original slots. It need not use a failed record identity. collect/rearm/start retain the preceding observer exclusions. No native action was added to drop_record and no queue/executor/generation registry was introduced.

specific_entry_point_assessment.cancel_destructors: Both old Ticket and old Draft idempotently lose native control before any route slot can be collected/rearmed. Their later drops cannot cancel a current episode.
specific_entry_point_assessment.fatal_paths: Both public explicit wait and poll/take revoke owned copies on terminal diagnostics other than Unavailable, retaining the first candidate error and original native retirement ownership.
specific_entry_point_assessment.retry_paths: Both diagnostic Unavailable and genuine ReadLease exclusivity rejection retain current ownership/live state; retry does not submit another copy.
specific_entry_point_assessment.closed_multiobserver: Closed store rejects new work before pinning; already-admitted observers retain native handles. Last observer removal permits existing collection, while a stale record can never reacquire a cleared owner.
specific_entry_point_assessment.handle_lifetimes: Tests keep endpoint Queue, Context and CopyObservation at stable addresses until route/native owner destruction. wait-thread Status is read only after join; the prior observer gate still establishes pin admission before concurrent store actions.

tests.red_scope: Root recorded one sequential real CPU F2 case with 23 failures against unchanged old product. This is historical reproduction, not a final run of all new tests.

new_tests.name: StateClone.OldFailedControlsCannotObserveOrCancelAReusedCopySlot
new_tests.assessment: Six old operations (wait/poll/ticket cancel/drop/draft cancel/drop) execute after accepted slot reuse. Native wait/cancel counters, current active count, successful real payload publication and another subsequent no-rearm clone expose the original corruption.

new_tests.name: StateClone.FailedNativeObservationRevokesOwnershipBeforeColdRearm
new_tests.assessment: Separately tests explicit wait and poll/take fatal boundaries. Wrapper returns one DataLoss only after original CPU wait succeeds; the error remains on the old record and later old controls cannot access current native handles.

new_tests.name: StateClone.UnavailableExclusiveOutputRetainsTheSameCopyForRetry
new_tests.assessment: Original F2 output supplies an extra real ReadLease. Original try_write rejects exclusivity until that reader is released; same ticket then publishes actual changed bytes without cancellation.

new_tests.name: StateClone.UnavailableNativeObservationKeepsItsAcceptedSlotForRetry
new_tests.assessment: Separate wait/poll entries see one wrapper Unavailable after actual CPU wait success. collect/rearm leave the accepted slot active, another draft cannot replace it, and same-ticket retry records one native copy.

tests.existing_observer_regression: Deterministic pin/gate/cancel/close test is preserved; guard wrapper still records and withholds overlapping native accesses instead of executing undefined native concurrency.
tests.after_execution: Not run by this reviewer; root owns incremental build and actual focused CPU result.

limits: No GPU, Vulkan, Apple, hardware-pending or end-model performance result is established by these CPU wrappers.

Injected DataLoss/Unavailable change one observation diagnostic after a genuine CPU copy. They are not claims that native CPU copying or a GPU kernel actually failed or remained pending. The separate exclusivity test uses the real original lease failure.

The persistent-native-Unavailable safety argument is source-level control-flow review: every failure exits before output publication. The transient test does not represent all native error recovery behaviors.
This fixes the identified finite copy-slot ownership root cause; it does not claim all future state/resource/concurrency defects are exhausted.

existing_root_expected_red.result: Original observer-fixed product object plus one fresh test TU actually exited1, one case with23 failures; product source was unchanged at reproduction.

new_tests.name: StateClone.OldFailedControlsCannotObserveOrCancelAReusedCopySlot
new_tests.coverage: Six sequential old-control operations: wait/poll/ticket cancel/ticket destruction/draft cancel/draft destruction. A new accepted same-slot copy remains active across collect and publishes real bytes; a subsequent clone needs no extra rearm. Native wait/cancel counters expose erroneous cross-episode access.

new_tests.name: StateClone.FailedNativeObservationRevokesOwnershipBeforeColdRearm
new_tests.coverage: The transparent original-CPU F2 wrapper reports one DataLoss after original wait succeeds, separately through poll/take and explicit wait. The first candidate retains that exact failure; after actual retirement/rearm old controls cannot touch the new accepted copy.

new_tests.name: StateClone.UnavailableExclusiveOutputRetainsTheSameCopyForRetry
new_tests.coverage: An additional real ReadLease returned by original CPU F2 output prevents the original try_write from obtaining exclusivity. Unavailable keeps the same owner/live copy; release the extra reader and poll the same ticket to publish without cancellation, re-copy or cold rearm.

new_tests.name: StateClone.UnavailableNativeObservationKeepsItsAcceptedSlotForRetry
new_tests.coverage: The transparent real-CPU F2 wrapper returns one Unavailable after original wait success, through both poll/take and explicit wait. Collect/rearm cannot retire/replace that accepted copy, another draft cannot claim its slot, and the same ticket can retry without another native submission. This models an observation boundary, not measured GPU readiness.

test_design.existing_preserved: Original observer-close deterministic regression, schema-extent fix and all original StateVersions/StateClone neighbors remain in the source.
limits: Only root executed the recorded first reproduction. No final compile/test or any GPU/backend run was performed by this implementation agent.

The DataLoss/Unavailable wrapper changes only one observation diagnostic after the original CPU copy; it is not an independently failed native GPU kernel, measured hardware pending state or a second executor. Actual native errors remain checked and cannot turn into success by this product change.
The Unavailable case uses actual original output-reader exclusivity; no arbitrary pending outcome or fake lease is substituted.

No public generation API or StateRecord layout change is introduced. TypedStateCopy keeps its original live Submission on Unavailable instead of freeing a slot whose public owner remains valid; fatal native status cleanup is unchanged.
Actual Windows CPU only. No CUDA/Vulkan/Apple pending native run, model validation, GPU profile or throughput result for this batch.

DataLoss/Unavailable diagnostics are transparent test-only observation boundaries after original CPU wait success. They do not prove a failing GPU kernel, hardware pending timing or recovery of a cached native failure; actual native errors remain checked.
The separate Unavailable reader test uses an actual additional original F2 output ReadLease and genuine try_write exclusivity, then retries the same copy without resubmission.
The independent source review and these focused cases do not prove all cross-platform State lifetime or the full inference architecture complete.
No executable/object/library/map payloads or cleanup suggestions/receipts are included in the archive. No files were deleted while publishing.
